summary: Sawyer County, WI tower in the Town of Sand Lake; FFLA lists it standing, it was one of five DNR towers in the county, and it helped in a 1966 crash response.

facts.status_note: FFLA lists it as standing; the DNR planned to take its towers out of service (2016 per the Sawyer County Record, 2015 per WJFW); no recent condition report found
facts.agency: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources (per Sawyer County Record)

events.note: A part-time fire-watcher named Langham climbed the tower to help direct first responders to a bomber crash near unincorporated Hauer in Sawyer County
Bomber from Barksdale Air Force Base, on a low-level mission over Ladysmith, clipped treetops and crashed in timber near unincorporated Hauer in Sawyer County; the tower was used in the response
DNR said its 72 fire towers, including five in Sawyer County, would be taken out of service in 2016; WJFW says they were decommissioned in 2015

evidence.quote: Towers in Sawyer County include Hayward, located south of Hayward; another in the Town of Sand Lake; one in the middle of the county, Pipestone; and two in the lower half of the county: Swayne, between the villages of Radisson and Winter, and Connors Lake on the border of Price County.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Sawyer County Record says the DNR would take its towers out of service in 2016; WJFW says the 72 towers were decommissioned in 2015. The story gives both and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: The 1966 crash response (crash near unincorporated Hauer, Sawyer County, per UW-Madison) and the DNR retirement context are sourced. No source gives this tower's build date, builder, condition or access, so none is stated. FFLA's key marks towers whose cab is gone with an asterisk; this entry has none, so the cab is presumably present, but no source says so directly.
